The scope discussed in the log management chapter pertains to operational logs related to maintenance, excluding redo/archive log files related to data. Management of redo/archive log files will be described in the file management chapter.

## Log Classification

The classification of operational logs in YashanDB is as follows:

*   **Run Log**: The run log records track information generated by various database services, debugging information, state transitions, potential issues that did not impact performance, and direct error information.
*   **Alert Log**: When errors such as deadlock, full tablespace, network disconnection, or bad blocks occur, the database may run in a "degraded state." Maintenance personnel should be informed of these issues promptly for resolution. The database raises alerts in the alert log (reporting alert events). Maintenance personnel can monitor the alert log regularly to prevent issues and stay informed about the system's performance. All alert event information contained in YashanDB is detailed in the reference manual [Alert Events](../../../参考手册/告警事件).
*   **Listener Log**: When the database experiences problems like connection storms, connection sources need to be examined for troubleshooting. The listener log provides maintenance personnel with information on connection status and frequency.
*   **Slow Log**: The slow log, officially known as the Slow Query Log, is primarily used to record SQL statements that exceed a specified execution time in the database. It can be output to log files or system tables. The slow query log allows for identifying poorly performing statements for optimization purposes. The slow log is not suitable for ISC Distributed Cluster Deployment.
*   **Proxy Program Log (yex_server.log)**: Records the trace information, debugging information, state transitions, potential issues without impact, and direct error messages generated during the operation of services such as the yex_sever process hosting external UDF agent programs and DBLink.

The table below lists the corresponding file information for the above logs:

|Log File |Log Content |Description |
|--------------------------------------|-----|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| $YASDB_HOME/log/cluster_name/node-nodeid/run/run.log | Run Log | 1. Created by default at this path and name during installation.<br>2. The file path can be modified using the RUN_LOG_FILE_PATH parameter; if the path does not exist, it will automatically be created. Ensure the user has the appropriate privileges for the path.<br>3. The filename cannot be modified.     |
| $YASDB_DATA/log/alert/alert.log     | Alert Log | 1. Created by default at this path and name during installation.<br>2. The file path cannot be modified.<br>3. The filename cannot be modified.  
| $YASDB_DATA/log/listener/listener.log | Listener Log | 1. Created by default at this path and name during installation.<br>2. The file path cannot be modified.<br>3. The filename cannot be modified.  
| $YASDB_HOME/log/cluster_name/node-nodeid/slow/slow.log | Slow Query Log | 1. Created by default at this path and name during installation.<br>2. The file path can be modified using the SLOW_LOG_FILE_PATH parameter; if the path does not exist, it will automatically be created. Ensure the user has the appropriate privileges for the path.<br>3. The filename can be modified using the SLOW_LOG_FILE_NAME parameter.<br>4. If the output method is FILE, the entry will be recorded in this file; if TABLE, it will be recorded in the system table. |
| $YASDB_DATA/log/external/server/yex_server.log | Proxy Program Log | 1. Created by default at this path and name during installation.<br>2. The file path cannot be modified.<br>3. The filename cannot be modified. |

## Log Archiving

The table below lists the log types supported for archival in YashanDB:

|Log Type |Support Status |
|------| -------- |
| Run Log | Supported     |
| Alert Log | Not Supported   |
| Listener Log | Not Supported   |
| Slow Log  | Not Supported   |
| Proxy Program Log | Supported |

> **Caution**: 
>
> For logs that do not support archiving, database administrators should set up a regular cleaning strategy to avoid filling up disk space.

### Run Log Archiving

When the run log file reaches RUN_LOG_FILE_SIZE (default is 20M), it will be archived, and a new log file will be created. The archived log file will be named by appending the time suffix to the original log file name, such as: run/run-20211213151402.log.

### Proxy Program Log Archiving

When the proxy program log file reaches 16M, it will be archived, and a new log file will be created. The archived log file will be named by appending the time suffix to the original log file name, for example, external/server/yex_server20211213151402.log.

## Log Format

### Run Log File Content Format

The format is: date + time + [level] + [module] + log information. For example:

```verilog
2021-12-13 14:51:23.342 [INFO] [TABLESPACE] succeed to create tablespace SYSTEM
2021-12-13 14:53:18.559 [WARN] [CKPT] checkpoint not complete
2021-12-13 14:53:22.483 [DEBUG] [HA] send redo from point 0-5-12840-18360, size 278528, standby 1, next send point 0-5-12908-18373
```

**Log Level**

YashanDB run logs support different levels of log management and print logs according to the configuration:

|Level |Description |
| ----- | ---------------------------- |
| OFF   | Logs are disabled              |
| FATAL | Logs related to fatal errors   |
| ERROR | Logs related to general errors  |
| WARN  | Logs related to warning errors  |
| INFO  | Normal operation logs (default log level) |
| DEBUG | Debug log level                |
| TRACE | Trace logs                     |
| ALL   | All logs                       |

From top to bottom, the log levels increase; higher log levels include those of lower log levels.

### Alert Log File Content Format

The format is: TimeStamp | Session ID | Event Name | Object | Action | Content | Event Description. The descriptions of each field are as follows:

|Field |Type |Description |
| ----------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| TimeStamp   | timestamp | The time when the alert was generated                       |
| Session ID  | uint16    | The session ID that generated the alert                     |
| Event Name  | text      | The name of the alert type                                  |
| Object      | uint16    | The object ID that generated the alert <br>* Object and Event Name together constitute the unique identifier for the alert <br>* Some alerts do not require Object information, resulting in this value being 0 |
| Action      | int       | The state of the alert: <br>* 0: Alert triggered <br>* 1: Alert cleared |
| Content     | text      | Additional information related to the alert                 |
| Description | text      | Detailed information for the user to further understand the alert |

### Listener Log File Content Format

An example of the log format is as follows:

```verilog
2023-08-02 09:47:26.143 protocal = TCP  ip = fc00:7::126 port = 14526 user = SYS status = SUCCESS
2023-08-02 09:47:26.151 protocal = TCP  ip = fc00:7::126 port = 14528 user = SYS status = SUCCESS
2023-08-02 09:50:42.005 protocal = TCP  ip = fc00:7::126 port = 14650 user = SYS status = SUCCESS
2023-08-02 09:51:34.354 protocal = TCP  ip = fc00:7::126 port = 44058 user = REGRESS status = ERROR
2023-08-02 09:54:32.526 protocal = TCP  ip = fc00:7::126 port = 14656 user = SYS status = SUCCESS
2023-08-02 09:56:32.126 protocal = IPC  user = SYS status = SUCCESS
```

The format is:

TimeStamp | Protocal | Ip | Port | User | Status

|Field |Description |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| TimeStamp | The time when the listener record was generated         |
| Protocol  | Connection type<br />* TCP: TCP connection<br />* IPC: IPC connection |
| Ip        | Client IP                                              |
| Port      | Client PORT                                            |
| User      | Connecting user                                        |
| Status    | Connection status<br />* SUCCESS: Connection succeeded<br />* ERROR: Connection failed |

### Slow Log Content Format

**Slow Log File Format**

***Example*** is as follows:

```verilog
# TIME: 2022-11-18 20:51:30.374
# USER_HOST: SYS@127.0.0.1
# DB_NAME: test_base1
# COST_EXECUTE_TIME: 0.000119
# COST_OPTIMIZE_TIME: 0.000040
# ROWS_SENT: 1
# SQL_ID: 3jd5aq4g9t7gf
SQL: select * from v$parameter where name = 'SLOW_LOG_SQL_MAX_LEN'
```

The format is:

|Field |Description |
| --------- |----------------|
| TIME | The time when the slow SQL information was printed |
| USER_HOST  | Connection information when executing the SQL  |
| DB_NAME    | Database name used                        |
| COST_EXECUTE_TIME  | Time spent executing the SQL, in seconds     |
| COST_OPTIMIZE_TIME   | Time spent in the SQL optimization phase, in seconds |
| ROWS_SENT    | Number of rows returned                   |
| SQL_ID    | SQL ID          |

**Slow Log System Table Format**

The name of the slow log system table is SLOW_LOG$, and its structure is defined as follows:

|Column Name |Description |
|---------------|------------------------------|
| DATABASE_NAME    | Database name                   |
| USER_NAME        | Username                        |
| START_TIME       | The time when the log was recorded, not the start time of execution |
| USER_HOST        | Connection IP                   |
| QUERY_TIME       | Execution time                  |
| ROWS_SENT        | Number of rows returned         |
| SQL_ID           | SQL ID                          |
| SQL_TEXT         | SQL statement, truncated if over 2000 |
| SQL_FULLTEXT     | Complete SQL statement, enabled when SLOW_LOG_SQL_MAX_LEN is 0 |
| SQL_PARAMS       | All binding parameters of the SQL, separated by commas, can hold up to 64KB of data |

## Collecting Logs

The *yasboot* command can be used to collect logs from all nodes with one click. By default, it packages the logs from the nodes on the remote server and sends them to the current directory of the local server. You can customize the log storage directory using the -o parameter. For specific parameters and their meanings, please refer to [yasboot](../../../工具手册/yasboot/yasboot命令介绍/yasboot cluster).

```shell
yasboot cluster log -c yashandb
start:  2023-07-28 00:00:00
end  :  2023-07-28 20:11:19
+-------+------------------+-------------+----------+---------------------------+---------+-------------+----------+------+
| type  | uuid             | name        | hostid   | index                     | status  | return_code | progress | cost |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| task  | 05fc032f6cc54f69 | LogCollect  | -        | yashandb                  | SUCCESS | 0           | 100      | 4    |
+-------+------------------+-------------+----------+---------------------------+---------+-------------+----------+------+
| child | 74413dd89a9de397 | LogCompress | host0001 | host0001                  | SUCCESS | 0           | 100      | 1    |
|       +------------------+-------------+----------+---------------------------+---------+-------------+----------+------+
|       | bd728249e323192e | LogDownload | host0001 | host0001                  | SUCCESS | 0           | 100      | 1    |
|       +------------------+-------------+----------+---------------------------+---------+-------------+----------+------+
|       | d08b47e74604478a | LogCombine  | -        | yashandb-05fc032f6cc54f69 | SUCCESS | 0           | 100      | 1    |
+-------+------------------+-------------+----------+---------------------------+---------+-------------+----------+------+
task completed, status: SUCCESS
download log to /var/lib/jenkins/anchorbase/work/bin
downloading...
download file block size: 2097152
```
